subtopics.title: Diaspora Schemes: PIO and OCI
subtopics.summary: The OCI scheme was introduced in 2005 through an amendment to the Citizenship Act, 1955, and was merged with the PIO scheme in 2015. PIO card holders need no visa to visit India for 15 years from the date of issue of the card. OCI holders get a multipurpose, multiple-entry, lifelong visa and are exempt from police reporting.
facts: OCI scheme introduced in 2005 via amendment to the Citizenship Act, 1955
PIO and OCI schemes merged in 2015
PIO: a foreign citizen, except nationals of Pakistan, Afghanistan, Bangladesh, China, Iran, Bhutan, Sri Lanka and Nepal
PIO: a parent, grandparent or great-grandparent was born in and a permanent resident of India, or the person is a spouse of an Indian citizen or PIO
PIO card holders need no visa for 15 years from the date of issue of the card
PIO stay up to 180 days is exempt from FRRO/FRO registration; longer stays must register within 30 days
OCI eligibility covers persons eligible for Indian citizenship on 26.01.1950 and their minor children
Persons who were ever citizens of Pakistan or Bangladesh are not eligible for OCI
OCI holders get a multipurpose, multiple-entry, lifelong visa and are exempt from police reporting
OCI holders have no right to acquire agricultural or plantation properties

subtopics.title: Sri Lanka Profile and Strategic Context
subtopics.summary: Colombo is the executive capital of Sri Lanka and Sri Jayawardenepura Kotte houses the legislature, with Harini Amarasuriya as Prime Minister and Anura Kumara Dissanayake as President. The LTTE, formed in 1976, and the 13th Amendment shape Sri Lanka's internal politics. China's growing presence through financial aid and Hambantota Port raises strategic concerns for India.
facts: Capital: Colombo (Executive) and Sri Jayawardenepura Kotte (Legislature)
PM: Harini Amarasuriya; President: Anura Kumara Dissanayake
LTTE was formed in 1976 as a self-styled 'National Freedom Movement of People of Tamil Eelam'
LTTE undertook terrorist activities in Sri Lanka, especially against Sinhalese
13th Amendment of the Sri Lankan Constitution led to Provincial Councils with power-sharing for all 9 provinces
China's influence grows through financial aid and Hambantota Port
Chinese vessels Shi Yan-6 and Yuan Wang-5 conduct data collection, potentially supporting military operations against India
Multilateral forums include BIMSTEC, SAARC, Colombo Security Conclave and Indian Ocean Rim Association
